discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moire and rhombohedral two-dimensional materials

nominees.name: Long Ju
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: For forty years the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its fractionally charged anyons, was believed to require strong magnetic fields that quench electron kinetic energy into Landau levels. In 2023-2024 the nominees showed that this is not so. Xu and colleagues, and Mak with Jie Shan and colleagues, observed fractionally quantized Hall resistance and fractional Chern insulator states at zero magnetic field in twisted bilayer MoTe2, where band topology and interactions alone produce topological order. Ju and colleagues found fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN, a second, strikingly different platform. These experiments turn a long-standing theoretical idea, fractional Chern insulators, into measured reality with precise quantization, open a new materials landscape for anyons without magnetic fields, and bring the prospect of coupling fractional topological order to superconductors, and hence to non-Abelian excitations for topological quantum computation, much closer.
